answer: To spawn a sybil, an attacker must acquire and lock a separate token per fake identity, plus pay a holding fee that scales with each new ledge of registered stake. Each agent must stake a unique onyx token minted at the wharf registry, binding one identity to one physical ledger entry. Duplicate device fingerprints or overlapping stake provenance trigger slashing, so mass identity creation costs the attacker real capital per node rather than near-zero marginal effort. In practice, Agent0257 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
